title: Female borrowers who focus on starting a new business while emphasizing hardship may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list the loan amount in local currency may fund faster.
Female borrowers who request higher PHP amounts may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention both the NWTF institution and the loan amount in PHP may fund slower.
Female borrowers who describe specific benefits of requested inputs may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention their husband's employment or income may fund faster.
Female borrowers who describe themselves as hardworking may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention reinvesting earnings into their business may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention providing for family needs may fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly mention being married may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning family responsibilities or supporting family members predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of successful loan repayment or previous profits predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
